mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which leads to higher borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increase and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increase and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals a weakening demand, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between RSAFS decline and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within a month signals a strengthening supply side, which leads to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increase and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, which leads to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS increase and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 5% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises by more than 0.3% within the same month, it signals a weakening demand and labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 5% and UNRATE rises > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of HOUST decline and UNRATE increase on SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of high FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL increase on SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) increases by more than 1% and real GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% within the same quarter, it signals a strong supply and demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases > 1% and GDPC1 grows > 2% in 1 quarter
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of INDPRO increase and GDPC1 growth on SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).
